otherProject.title: Tajrīd Comparative Critical Sourcebook
otherProject.warning: The source counts are records and named works, NOT independently collated full Arabic commentaries.

purpose: Prevent translation duplication; each project has a different historical question.
transferRules: Tajrīd owns Ṭūsī matn, identical lemma, original objection/reply, Qūshjī/Jurjānī/Ḥillī/Lāhījī gloss critical translation and Dawwānī–Dashtakī exchange.

Late Avicennism owns the historical aftermath: how ontology, causality, natural philosophy, cognition, soul and divine agency were independently reformulated in later works after Asfār and the Tajrīd commentary tradition.
Shared overlapping lemmata are pointers into Tajrīd, not another extracted primary translation.
Do not automatically classify all Tajrīd witnesses as primary checked; preserve project status.
The current 20 late-reader historical records include texts by earlier authors as backgrounds, not twenty post-Asfar primary sources.
Identical author ≠ identical work: Lāhījī's Gawhar and Sarmaya are independent from Sharh al-Tajrid; link but do not conflate.

records.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
records.relation: same historical work; some exact loci may overlap
records.editorialRule: Tajrīd project owns lemma-level Tawsi → Lahiji quotation/commentary critical translation. Late Avicennism uses source as antecedent/bridge only; no second independent Lahiji translation unless a new non-overlapping argument or post-Ṣadrian shift is demonstrated.

records.author: Muḥammad Jaʿfar al-Astarābādī (reports Ṭūsī, Qūshjī, al-Khafrī, al-Khwānsārī)
records.relation: same historical work and divine-power controversy
records.editorialRule: Tajrīd owns cited Astarabadi verses/reply chain and attribution of Qushji/Khafri/Khwānsāri. Late Avicennism discusses what the controversy implies for later divine will and complete-cause theories; source reports linked not recopied.

records.author: Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī
records.relation: same Sharh al-Maqasid work; mental-existence debate overlaps
records.editorialRule: Tajrīd owns base scholastic lemma and critical passages in mental existence; Late Avicennism can compare later mind/body and second-intention transformations once independently sourced.

records.author: al-Ījī / al-Jurjānī / unnamed marginal layers
records.relation: same Sharh al-Mawaqif witness family; composite gloss source
records.editorialRule: Tajrīd owns matn/sharh/marginal textual collation; Late Avicennism treats further epistemology and the difference between mental form and independently external entity, without claiming new Siyalkuti readings.
